blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Structure a discursive piece dialectically: a thesis, its antithesis, and a synthesis; set counterarguments beside your points and answer them.

blocks.heading: Two variants, one task
blocks.text: Discursive writing explores an issue from more than one side before reaching a view; argumentative writing argues for one position and answers the other side. The variant the task’s wording signals: "explore", "consider" and "both sides" point to the first; "argue", "make the case" and a named position point to the second — and the wording is decoded before a word is written. The task is one of Section B’s category selection, set as 600–900 words for twenty-five marks.

blocks.heading: Dialectical structure
blocks.text: Dialectical structure is thesis, antithesis, synthesis: the case, its strongest opposition, and the reasoned view that survives the collision. Planning the piece means giving the opposition its strongest form — not its weakest — because a synthesis earned against the best counterargument is worth having, and one earned against a straw man convinces no one who held the objection. The plan marks three rooms: the thesis with its reasons, the antithesis voiced fairly, and the synthesis that gives ground where ground is owed and holds the line where the case stands.

blocks.heading: The four forms
blocks.text: The forms the question takes are the article, the essay, the speech and the letter to an editor. The article carries a headline and subheadings and addresses a magazine’s readership; the essay is continuous prose for a class or a publication that expects prose; the speech finds its hall, signposts its route and closes on its ask; the letter addresses the editor, quotes the claim it answers and signs off. Each convention set is part of the brief — writing an article with subheadings when an essay was set breaks the brief as visibly as writing 900 words of poem.

blocks.heading: Worked example: a dialectical plan
blocks.text: A task sets an article exploring whether homework should be abolished. The plan: thesis — homework done well works (the reason: practice consolidates; the example: the two-week spellings experiment in the plan’s writer’s own class; the consequence: learners who keep it keep the gain). Antithesis — the strongest case against (the reason: homework measures the home, not the learner; the example: the learner with the quiet room against the learner with the shift-working parent; the consequence: the practice that consolidates for one humbles the other). Synthesis — abolish the homework that measures homes, keep the homework that consolidates: set it shorter, set it smarter, and let the school day carry the practice. Three rooms, one door at the end.

blocks.heading: Where the pieces are marked
blocks.text: The twenty-five marks of this category are the same five strands as the whole of Section B: expression and range, accuracy, organisation and development, task achievement, and the audience held — and the dialectical structure serves the last three of them directly. The organisation strand rewards the thesis-antithesis-synthesis shape; the development strand rewards the reasons, examples and consequences inside each room; and the audience strand rewards the fairness of a piece that met its opposition instead of hiding it. The plan is not extra work beside the writing: it is the writing’s marks, arranged in advance.

blocks.heading: Three failures of the brief
blocks.text: The first failure is the one-sided list: reasons for, reasons for, reasons for, and a one-line conclusion — the argument that never happened, because the reader who held the objection leaves holding it still. The second is narrowing gone wrong: the wording names a whole civilisation and the piece takes it all on, thinning every section, when the writing should take one part and let the whole be visible behind it. The third is the wrong form: an article’s subheadings in an essay, a speech that never addresses its hall. Each failure is checked the same way — reread the brief, and test the plan against variant, scope and form.
